  • What it sounds like: A dry, punchy unison bass: every voice stacked on one note, fat and thick, loosened just enough that the stack breathes without ever going seasick. Warm, with a driven edge that stops short of fuzz, and each note is chopped hard on release: no spring, no echo, no tail, only the silence after the hit. It has presence: it sits forward and fills the room.
  • Sound design notes: Low register. Roots and octaves from about A1 to A2 are the sweet spot, for single-note bass lines and chopped roots; the very bottom (A0 and the low end of A1) is partly below what small speakers and many PAs reproduce, so on a laptop you hear the body, not the floor. Staccato to medium — eighth-note chops (roughly 130 ms) are home — and it also holds as a wall of low unison with a slow, controlled beat. It is a unison: one note at a time, no chords. Tricks: ALGORITHM loosens the stack further; Tape Stop dives the whole low stack; the kill switch stops it dead; per-voice DRIVE (MIXER page, knob 4) is the gentle route to more grit, while GROWL is a big step (nothing below about 28, compressing past about 40). Effects are at 0 on purpose (dry and punchy is the sound; a wash will blur the chop). It deliberately sits about 1.5 dB above the bank's usual level for presence — expect it to jump out a little when you switch to it. On the FM-1 (12 Nov), with all four Psych Chain effects pushed hard, four notes held read about 5600 µs against the 5800 µs budget in the source (Vincent's reading, ±100): the highest of the six patches he read, so it is the one to watch when riding the effects hard.
  • 31 Fi(l)fth — VOICED (4–5 Nov 2026, approved as is; variant C, the DUAL stab). The archetypal aggressive chord stab. Directly the top-voted DØG-5 sound.
  • What it sounds like: A fifth built into every note, a hard filter pluck, and a short slap-back echo right behind it. Each note is a detuned pair, so it is fat and punchy rather than thin, warm rather than icy, with a bright snap on the front that settles into a solid body. Dry apart from the slap: no spring, no long wash, just the stab and its quick echo.
  • Sound design notes: Low to low-mid register; single notes and fifth-based riffs (roots and octaves around A1 to A2) are home ground — every note already carries its own fifth, so one finger plays a power chord. Short and hard: a stab of roughly 150–200 ms (there is no gate-length control; the stab is as long as you hold the key). Chords, honestly: because the fifth is built into every voice, chords of fifths stack fifths on fifths into sus2-style clusters — the engine doing what the patch asks. Every note is two voices, so chords are three notes by design (three notes use six voices; a fourth still fits, using all eight; a fifth steals). It is heavier on CPU than a single-voice stab. The slap (ALLEY) is on and is what makes it the Space-Echo stab; turn ALLEY up on the BBD DELAY page for a longer echo. Other tricks untested on this patch; a spring will blur the stab.
  • 32 Init bruv? — VOICED (11 Nov 2026, approved after listening; variant B). The blank slate that closes the bank.
  • What it sounds like: A plain voice made of two saw waves played through a low-pass filter with a short envelope, dry, with chords and single notes both playable. Nothing is added to it: no modulation, no echo, no spring, no tape and no drive.
  • Sound design notes: It is the engine's own default program with one change, VOLUME 97 (the default is 100). It is not a single raw saw with an open filter: POLY 5, two saws 4.7 cents apart, a 24 dB low-pass at CUTOFF 80 with RESO 20, a filter envelope and an amp envelope, VINTAGE 30, SPREAD 60, every effect at 0. Slots 33–99 hold the same defaults as INIT, with VOLUME 100. Chords play (POLY 5); −18.05 dBFS RMS on the stabs phrase, peak −5.6 dBFS. With GROWL, DLY MIX, DRAIN and CHEW at 0 the audio was bit-identical when every other effect control was moved to its extreme. About 1814 host instr/sample worst case. A raw single-saw render ("Craw") and a MONO init stay on the listening branch as v1.1 candidates for more blank canvases.

PART 4 — GEAR INSPIRATIONS

For each voiced patch: real-world instruments and pedals whose character it draws on, each tagged with the dictionary trait it carries — so "a bit more Mono/Poly" translates straight into parameter moves. These are inspirations, not imitations: nothing here is modelled, ripped or sampled, and gear names appear only in this manual — never in patch names or on-screen text. All trademarks belong to their owners; DØG-5 is not affiliated with or endorsed by any of them. A tag is kept only where the final patch carries the trait; traits the patch lacks are named as such.

Each entry ends with a Closest to line: the one instrument you would name if someone asked "what does it sound like?"

Chapter I — JALOPY

01 Red Pill

  • Korg MS-20 — the resonant filter and its bite. Nasty, biting, resonant.
  • Minimoog — the stacked saws. Fat, thick.
  • Roland SH-101 — the tight snap at the front of a note. Tight, punchy.
  • ProCo RAT — the driven edge. Gritty, crunchy.
  • Closest to: an MS-20 bass through a RAT.

02 Cement Grind

  • Roland Juno-60 — the pulse-width movement. PWM, wobble, thick.
  • Korg Polysix — the stacked pulses. Fat, PWM.
  • Roland SH-101 — the punchy PWM bass. PWM bass, punchy.
  • ProCo RAT — the crunch. Crunchy.
  • Korg MS-20 — the filter. Biting.
  • Closest to: a Juno-60 PWM bass through a RAT.

03 Half-Life

  • Korg Mono/Poly — detuned oscillators that drift and never settle. Fat, slop, seasick, thick.
  • Sequential Prophet-5 (early, tuning-unstable revisions) — dual-saw warmth with the drift. Fat, warm, drift.
  • Minimoog — the body under the instability. Fat, sub-heavy, thick.
  • Korg MS-20 — the bite and the spit in the filter and the tail. Nasty, biting, spitting.
  • Closest to: Korg Mono/Poly — its drifting, detuned saw chaos, with Minimoog weight underneath, chopped by the gate.

04 V-Sync

  • Sequential Pro-One — the sync sweep itself. Sync, punchy, ripping.
  • Sequential Prophet-5 — the fatness of a doubled voice. Sync, fat.
  • ARP Odyssey — the nasal, cutting tone. Nasal, biting.
  • Moog Prodigy — the cheap, raw edge. Fat, cheap, raw.
  • Closest to: a Pro-One sync lead.

05 ZEAROX

  • Roland TR-808 kick — the thump. Sub, thump.
  • Roland SH-101 — the weight. Sub, thick.
  • Tascam Portastudio cassette 4-track — lo-fi squash. Lo-fi, noisy.
  • ProCo RAT — the overload. Crunchy, driven.
  • Closest to: an 808 kick smashed onto a blown-out cassette 4-track. (Honest note: the tape and the drive stage are not in the final patch — they were removed in round 2 at the owner's direction; what remains is the hard, two-level square.)

06 zzuFuzz

  • Death by Audio Fuzz War — the benchmark, a huge fuzz beast. Fuzzy, thick wall.
  • Electro-Harmonix Big Muff — the wall. Fuzzy, thick wall.
  • Fuzz Face — the fuzz. Fuzzy, spitting.
  • Univox Super-Fuzz — voltage-starved, spitting.
  • Korg Mono/Poly — as the source. Fat, drifting.
  • Realistic Concertmate MG-1 — voltage-starved, lo-fi.
  • Closest to: a Mono/Poly into a Big Muff. (Built toward the descriptions by measurement and approved by ear; nothing says it matches the benchmark, and the voltage-starved gating of the Super-Fuzz and MG-1 is not claimed.)

07 Tape Splice

  • Korg Mono/Poly — the cross-modulated fat square. Fat, drifting.
  • Sequential Prophet-5 — the nervous pitch wobble. Wobble, nervous.
  • Roland RE-201 Space Echo — the worn tape stage. Wobble, lo-fi.
  • Roland SH-101 — the clipped, punchy gate. Punchy.
  • Closest to: a Mono/Poly cross-mod square through a worn tape echo.

08 Wire Bite

  • Korg Mono/Poly (in unison) — the stack. Fat, drifting.
  • Minimoog — thick.
  • Korg MS-20 — the bite. The bite.
  • Roland Jupiter-4 — fat, wobble.
  • Sequential Prophet-5 (early revisions) — the unsteadiness. Drift.
  • Closest to: a Mono/Poly in unison with MS-20 bite.

  • Roland SH-101 — the tight, quick note. Tight, punchy.

  • Fender spring reverb tank — springy (DRAIN 70; louder than the chord for its first 250 ms or so).
  • Mellotron M400 — the reference for the tone that was being chased. Measured traits only: dark (centroid 562 Hz, muddiness ratio 315) and a slow beating between the two oscillators (13.6 dB at 0.9 Hz on one voice). "Warped, wobbly tape" and "soft flute-like tone" are not in this patch (the tape deck is off; harmonics 3 / 5 / 7 read −11 / −18 / −26 dB against a triangle's −19 / −28 / −34).

  • Roland TR-808 — thick sub (with the 299 ms attack the sub's 40–150 Hz band peaks 255 ms after the note-on and falls 20 / 40 dB in 58 / 70 ms after that peak; the 6 Nov version's shares are in the voice card; "booming" is not measured).
  • Simmons SDS-V — noise burst (the noise is 15.6 dB over the sub in the first 100 ms on A1, a window that now sits inside the attack; attack 10 / 50 / 90% at 25.2 / 126.2 / 208.0 ms; "crashing" is supported only by the band decay).
  • Roland RE-201 Space Echo — long repeats (361 ms, FEEDBK 100, MIX 80; 8 repeats above −40 dB; not a runaway).

  • Electro-Harmonix Deluxe Memory Man — BBD feedback with pitch modulation; Wet. 10 repeats above −40 dB, return to −40 dB in 1721 ms (measured). There is no pitch modulation inside the echo; the largest gap between a note and its own repeat is 212 cents (computed). "Seasick" is not measured: at 4.9 Hz it is a wobble.
  • Roland RE-201 Space Echo — echo feedback; Wash. The tail takes 4624 ms to fall 60 dB (measured). This patch does not self-oscillate (FEEDBK 95).
  • Korg Polysix — the ensemble-chorus dizziness; Wobble. A triangle pitch LFO at 4.9 Hz, ±178 cents (measured). Beating is not measured; there is no chorus in the patch.
  • Closest to: a soft triangle-like pad run through a Memory Man until it seasicks itself.

  • Sequential Prophet-5 — the classic sync solo; Sync, Ripping, Fat. Sync: OSC 2 is hard-synced to OSC 1 (a setting). Ripping: on notes 2–8 of the detached riff the centroid over the first 100 ms is 2935 Hz, 303 Hz above the same riff with the sweep off (measured). Fat: not measured, except that the three voices beat at 0.99 Hz with a 16.9 dB swing in the 220 Hz band on a held A3.
  • Sequential Pro-One — the sweep itself; Rip, Bright. The sweep is ENV>O2 104, +15.2 semitones at the envelope's top (computed). On a detached A3 the centroid runs 2662 / 1724 / 1111 Hz over 0–50 / 50–150 / 150–400 ms (measured). No comparison with the Pro-One was made.

  • ARP Odyssey — the nasal cut; Nasal, Biting. Not measured.
  • Closest to: a Prophet-5 sync lead pushed into crunch. ("Crunch" is Vincent's word; the measured fact is the crest factor, 6.0 dB with GROWL 44 against 11.7 dB without drive.)

27 R3V3RT

  • Roland SH-101 — the tight, quick note; Tight, Punchy. Key-up to −20 / −40 / −60 dB is 11 / 15 / 19 ms on A2 (measured; the 9 ms meter window is the floor of these readings). Punchy: not measured.
  • Minimoog — the round immediate low end; Round, Thick. Not measured. The band shares are measured: on A2 the first 400 ms are 1 / 82 / 9 / 6 / 1 % in <60 / 60–150 / 150–400 / 400–1.2k / 1.2k+ Hz.
  • Moog Prodigy — the plain pulse; Raw, Fat. A single pulse (OSC 1 PW 54, OSC 2 off); "raw" and "fat" are not measured.
  • Sequential Pro-One — the snap of the filter decay; Snappy. On A2 the filter snap peaks at a centroid of 2891 Hz and lasts 175 ms; the centroid reads 2828 / 1759 / 440 Hz over 0–20 / 20–100 / 100–300 ms (measured). No comparison with the Pro-One was made.
  • Closest to: an SH-101 pulse bass with a Minimoog body.

28 Arr 2 Dee 2

  • Yamaha DX7 (tubular-bells voice) — FM clang, inharmonic. Partly carried: OSC 2 sits +15 semitones above OSC 1 (a ratio of 2.38) and feeds OSC 1 by X-MOD 32. At A4 in the first 300 ms that partial reads 1.197 × the prime at −11.1 dB. Not carried: DX7-style operators (this is one saw modulating another). "Clang" is not measured.
  • Roland D-50 ("Fantasia") — crystalline. Not carried. The engine has no per-partial envelope, so no partial outlasts the body. At A4 the share of energy above 4 kHz is 4.0% in the first 20 ms and 0.4% at 1–2 s.
  • Casio CZ-101 (phase-distortion bells) — a bright, bell-like phase-distortion tone. Not carried: the engine has no phase distortion; the sideband character here comes from X-MOD. Whether it resembles those bells is not measured.
  • A struck tubular or church bell — the classical partials. Carried, measured: the five classical partials of the ladder (hum 0.5, prime 1, tierce 1.2, quint 1.5, nominal 2) are all present, with the amplitudes in Part 3. "Church bell" is Vincent's word and is not measured.
  • Closest to: a DX7 tubular bell with a long, slowly moving tail.

29 i scream

  • Yamaha DX7 (tubular-bells voice) — FM clang, inharmonic. OSC 2 sits +15 semitones above OSC 1 (a ratio of 2.38) with X-MOD 25. Through the filter that partial reads −34 dB under the note at C#6 and −18 dB at C#5 (measured, first 100 ms), so it is faint at the top of the keybed. "Clang" is not measured.
  • A music box, struck — fast-decay, nostalgic. Not carried: the ring takes 1896 ms to fall 40 dB at C#6 (measured), a long ring. "Nostalgic" is Vincent's word and is not measured.
  • Finger cymbals (zills) — bright metallic ping. The centroid over the first 20 ms is 2096 Hz at C#6 and 1958 Hz at C#5 (measured). "Metallic" is not measured.
  • A transistor radio or van horn speaker — band-limited, honky, lo-fi. The filter read with white noise peaks at 1099 Hz, with a −3 dB width of 898–1345 Hz; 0.4% of its energy is under 400 Hz and 4.1% above 4 kHz (measured). "Lo-fi" is not measured.
  • Closest to: a music-box chime played through a cheap van horn speaker. Provenance: built by ear from Vincent's field recordings of a real ice-cream van; the measurements of the recordings were rough; nothing is sampled. Vincent's ear (not measured): closer to an arcade or vintage video-game chime.

32 Init bruv?

  • Sequential Prophet-5 — a plain saw, the filter open. Not carried: the filter is a 24 dB low-pass at CUTOFF 80 with RESO 20, and there are two saws, not one.
  • Minimoog — one raw oscillator. Not carried: OSC 2 is on (a saw, 4.7 cents from OSC 1).
  • Roland SH-101 — a saw, the filter open. Not carried, for the same two reasons.
